# The D board, live at 2026-09-22 10:38

**Generated by running the commands, not by writing a table.** Every count below is derived on that
run from `REF-the-d-numbers-what-each-one-means-and-which-are-only`’s [D-MAP] block and the state of
the items it names. Nothing here is stored, so nothing here can go stale — but this FILE is a
distillate and it freezes counts that keep moving. **Re-run the two commands rather than trusting
this page**, which is the defect this campaign measured six times:

    node src/cli/index.ts path --all
    node scripts/check-board.ts --orphans

Repository at `acd574ce`. Written to be correlated with
`reports/2026-09-21-v2-release-runbook.md`, whose triage is dated 2026-09-21.

## 1. The three totals do not agree, and that is the first thing to reconcile

| source | count | |
|---|---|---|
| the runbook’s headline (§7) | **160** | "the triage of the 160 open tasks" |
| the runbook’s own eight buckets, summed | **154** | 17 + 11 + 11 + 17 + 28 + 55 + 8 + 7 |
| the board, live today | **155** | `check-board`: 137 under subjects + 18 orphans |

**155 against the runbook’s 160 is explained and benign.** Five items were marked done today —
`rulings/101`, `/109`, `/111`, `/112`, `/113` — all of which shipped on 2026-09-17 and had never been
advanced. They were legitimately open when the runbook was written. 160 − 5 = 155.

**154 against 160 is NOT explained, and it is the gap worth your attention before the runbook runs.**
Six tasks are in the headline and in no bucket. The runbook’s stated intention is to close every open
issue systematically; a task in no bucket is in no phase, and a task in no phase is not closed by
running the plan. **Reconcile the buckets to the board before phase 2, not after.**

## 4. Twenty-one subjects read "open" with every item done

D8, D13a/b, D14, D16, D17, D20, D21, D22, D29, D31, D34, D35, D36, D38, D40, D42, D59, D65, D71,
D73, D74.

**A subject closes on a JUDGEMENT and never on a count**, which is why the tool refuses to close them
for you. For a release these are the cheapest thing on the board: each is a decision, not work. If
the runbook’s phase 2 closes only the 17 it names, these 21 stay open at 100%.

## 6. What this page does not tell you

  - **Whether a subject SHOULD close.** Only the judgement does that.
  - **Which runbook phase a given D falls in.** The runbook triages by task, this table aggregates by
    subject, and no column joins them — that join is the correlation you are about to do by hand.
  - **Anything about the 15 blockers.** B1–B15 are in the runbook §4; three were verified live today
    (B2 red, B15 mis-ordered, B6 absent) and the rest were not re-checked here.
